question: How does Base UI handle announced strings, and is that better or worse than React Aria's patchable bundles?
verdict: WORSE, on one string, for a structural reason. Base UI ships NO i18n layer of any kind — no locale bundles, no strings provider, no key namespace, no locale context. Seven of its eight announced English strings are reachable by prop, which is one MORE than React Aria manages by prop (5 of 8). The eighth, Combobox/Autocomplete's aria-label="Dismiss", is UNREACHABLE: it is an inline literal on an @internal component that accepts no props and sits under no provider. React Aria's identically-worded string has an address — the '@react-aria/overlays' registry, key 'dismiss' — which is exactly why patches/react-aria@3.51.0.patch already renders it as 'بستن'. Base UI's has no address, so there is no patch target: only a byte-rewrite of a component file, which cannot be locale-aware because no locale is in scope at that line. An unreachable hardcoded English string is worse than a patchable one.

versions.RENAMED_PACKAGE_WARNING: @base-ui-components/react is DEAD at 1.0.0-rc.0 (dist-tags.latest === '1.0.0-rc.0'). It is not this library at a lower version; it is the pre-rename name. Measuring it would produce numbers for a package nobody ships.

method.install: Added '@base-ui/react': 1.7.0 to pnpm-workspace.yaml catalog and packages/ui/package.json dependencies, then `pnpm install`. No shipped component imports it; it is present so its dist can be read. `tsc --noEmit` in packages/ui is green with it added.
method.static_census: Full-tree scan of all 789 .mjs files for (a) every aria-* attribute assigned a string literal, (b) every capitalised or multi-word string literal outside dev-warning machinery, (c) every template literal containing prose. Not a rendered sweep — a source scan sees strings inside portalled subtrees, which the SSR tier structurally cannot.
method.reachability: experiments/harness/probe.base-ui-i18n.mjs — renderToStaticMarkup over React.createElement, each carrier rendered bare and again with the Persian override, then grepped.
method.why_not_measure_mjs: measure.mjs grades Lumo's thirteen wrapped components against the shipped gate RULES and needs a specimens.base-ui.tsx that does not exist yet. This brief is one question and needed no wrappers. No gate number is reported here on purpose: the gate is the project's definition of a defect and reimplementing it in a probe would measure the probe. The probe records full HTML per arm so a later phase can grade it with the real rules.

limitations: STRING INVENTORY IS STATIC, REACHABILITY IS RENDERED. The eight strings come from a source scan of the dist; the prop/unreachable verdicts come from SSR renders. Where a carrier is portalled (Combobox.Popup's second dismiss sentinel, ComboboxPopup.mjs:115) the verdict is inherited from the same component's non-portalled instance (ComboboxInput.mjs:368), which does render on the server and is quoted below. That is an inference of one hop, and it is named so it can be checked.
NO GATE NUMBERS. packages/gate's RULES were not run over these renders. `no-latin-aria` would fire on the bare arms, but the count belongs to measure.mjs, which imports the real rules.

THE SCOPE DIFFERS FROM THE REACT ARIA FIGURE. React Aria's 8 came from a 25-component sweep of Lumo's actual surface. Base UI's 8 is a WHOLE-LIBRARY census across all 37 components it documents. Restricted to the thirteen files in experiments/baseline-rac/, Base UI leaks 6 (number-field 3, slider 2, combobox 1). Both numbers are given below; do not compare the 8s directly.

CLIENT-ONLY ANNOUNCEMENTS WERE NOT EXERCISED. Nothing here presses a key or opens a menu. The census would have found a hardcoded live-region string if one existed — it found none beyond the eight — but a string composed at interaction time from user data is out of scope by construction.

NATIVE FORM VALIDATION IS THE BROWSER'S, NOT BASE UI'S. field/root/useFieldValidation.mjs:201 reads `element.validationMessage`. Base UI ships zero validation copy of its own, which is the correct choice, but it means the message language follows the BROWSER UI language, not the page's lang. That is a platform property, not a Base UI defect, and it is not counted among the eight.

evidence: Zero files in the package match *i18n*, *locale*, *intl*, *translat*, *messages*, *strings* except utils/stringifyLocale.{mjs,d.ts}, which is `String(locale)` for a cache key — not a strings mechanism.

grep -rin 'i18n|localiz|localis|translation' across all 3240 files returns only CSS `translation` offsets, date-format token names, and the word 'translation' inside a toast doc paragraph. There is no i18n mention in the library, in its 78 shipped doc pages, or in its 111 KB CHANGELOG.
83 export subpaths (46 public + 37 ./internals/*). Exactly two are providers: ./csp-provider and ./direction-provider. Neither carries strings, and neither has a locale-shaped sibling.
The only translation-shaped thing in the whole package is `DirectionProvider`, and it carries a direction enum, not text.
i18n_layer.consequence: There is no bundle tier. React Aria's taxonomy has three rungs — prop, bundle, neither. Base UI's has two: prop, or nothing. Any string a prop does not reach is terminal.

locale_plumbing.mechanism: a per-component `locale?: Intl.LocalesArgument` prop, defaulting to undefined

components_declaring_locale.affects: the visible formatted value in the <input>
aria-valuetext digits and the formatted value on context
string COMPARISON only (the filter collator), not rendered text

locale_plumbing.default_when_omitted: the RUNTIME locale — `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, options)` in utils/formatNumber.mjs:12, which is Node's ICU default on the server and the browser's on the client. AriaCombobox.d.ts:207 says so in as many words: "Defaults to the user's runtime locale."
locale_plumbing.hazard: Forgetting the prop on one component out of four produces Latin digits on a Persian page with no error, no warning, and no type complaint — the exact silent-defect shape this repository's gate exists to catch. NumberFieldRoot.mjs:110 even sets `suppressHydrationWarning: true` on the input because server and client locales are expected to disagree, which removes the one signal React would otherwise have given. Contrast React Aria, where a single I18nProvider at the root reaches every descendant and there is nothing per-component to forget.

direction.mechanism: an explicit React context, DirectionProvider, read by useDirection()
evidence: direction-provider/DirectionProvider.mjs:13-15 — `const { direction = 'ltr' } = props;` (the destructure is emitted across three lines; the default is on :14)

Nothing in the library reads `document.dir`, an ancestor `dir` attribute, or a computed `direction` to derive it. The single `style.direction === 'rtl'` read in the tree is floating-ui-react/hooks/useDismiss.mjs:248, which detects which side the scrollbar is on during an outside-press, unrelated to component direction.

The shipped docs say it outright — docs/react/utils/direction-provider.md:148: "<DirectionProvider> enables child Base UI components to adjust behavior based on RTL text direction, but does not affect HTML and CSS. The dir=\"rtl\" HTML attribute or direction: rtl CSS style must be set additionally by your own application code."
direction.persian_or_rtl_specific_handling: none. There is no Persian anything: no fa locale, no Jalali calendar, no Arabic-script digit handling. Direction is a two-value enum and that is the whole of it. Both temporal adapters shipped (date-fns, luxon) are Gregorian-format-token adapters; neither is wired to a calendar system chooser.

it_changes_the_served_bytes.claim: direction is NOT a paint-time-only concern here — it changes server output, so getting it wrong is a defect the first byte already carries
it_changes_the_served_bytes.meaning: A Persian page that sets <html dir="rtl"> and forgets DirectionProvider renders every slider thumb offset by its own full width, in the served HTML, with correct-looking CSS around it.

other_behaviour_gated_on_the_same_defaul: internals/useAnchorPositioning.mjs:95-102 — 'inline-start'/'inline-end' resolve to left/right from useDirection(), so popovers, menus, selects and tooltips anchor to the wrong side
internals/composite/composite.mjs:47 and internals/composite/root/useCompositeRoot.mjs:110 — roving-focus arrow direction for every composite widget
direction.comparison_to_react_aria: React Aria has ONE lever. I18nProvider takes a locale and derives direction from it, so direction cannot disagree with the locale. Base UI has TWO independent levers — a per-component `locale` prop and a global `DirectionProvider` — plus the CSS `dir`, and nothing ties them together. A Lumo wrapper on Base UI would have to guarantee all three agree; nothing in the library would fail if they did not.

announced_strings.note_on_bundle_column: 0 is not a count of missed strings — it is the statement that the column does not exist. Base UI has no bundle, registry or key namespace to reach.

strings.why: NumberFieldInput.mjs:394 merges `props: [inputProps, elementProps, ...]` and merge-props/mergeProps.mjs:118 states 'In case of conflicts, the external props take precedence.' elementProps is the consumer's, and it is to the RIGHT of inputProps.
useNumberFieldStepperButton.mjs:165 merges `props: [props, elementProps, getButtonProps]`; internals/use-button/useButton.mjs sets no aria-label, so the consumer's value survives the last merge step.

strings.source: progress/root/ProgressRoot.mjs:43 — `let defaultAriaValueText = 'indeterminate progress';` used at :64 — `'aria-valuetext': getAriaValueText ? getAriaValueText(formattedValue, value) : defaultAriaValueText,`
strings.reaching_prop: getAriaValueText OR a literal aria-valuetext, both on Progress.Root
strings.caveat: In the indeterminate case `formattedValue` is the empty string, so a getAriaValueText callback receives '' and must know from context that it is being asked for the indeterminate phrasing. The prop reaches it; the SIGNATURE does not tell you which state you are in.

strings.trap: getAriaValueText is a THUMB prop, not a Root prop. Passed to Slider.Root it is not a prop at all: React forwards it to the DOM as an unknown attribute (dev warning only) and the English survives untouched. This is the same shape as CONTRIBUTING.md's warning about aria-roledescription sitting on NumberField's <input> rather than its <Group>. The probe pins both arms.
strings.worst_property: This is the ONLY one of the eight that is a HALF-localised string. The digits obey the `locale` prop and come out Persian; the words around them stay English. A reviewer who does not read Persian sees ۲۰ and assumes the string is handled. A single-thumb slider emits no aria-valuetext at all, so the defect appears only when a range slider is added.

strings.extra: It labels a role="region" with aria-live="polite" — the announced name of the live region itself.

strings.component: Combobox and Autocomplete — the internal dismiss sentinels
why_unreachable: The component's props argument is literally discarded: `function ComboboxInternalDismissButton(_, forwardedRef)` at ComboboxInternalDismissButton.mjs:14. It accepts no props, so there is no override to place.
The literal is written AFTER the spread — `...dismissProps, "aria-label": "Dismiss"` at :31-32 — so even a props path would lose to it.
It is marked `@internal` and is not in any of the 83 export subpaths, so it cannot be imported and shadowed either.

It is constructed by its parents, not composed by the consumer: ComboboxInput.mjs:368 renders one before the input, ComboboxPopup.mjs:115 renders a second after the popup. Neither forwards consumer props to it.
There is no provider, bundle or key to reach it through, because the library has none of those things.
strings.select_is_not_affected: Select composes its own popup and does not import ComboboxInternalDismissButton; the probe's select arm renders no Dismiss.
strings.observed_with_every_prop_tried: unchanged — aria-label on Combobox.Input renames the INPUT and leaves the sentinel English, which the probe shows side by side

the_decisive_comparison.react_aria_same_string: React Aria has the identical control and the identical word, and it is BUNDLE-reachable. dist/private/overlays/DismissButton.mjs:29 reads `let labels = useLabels(otherProps, stringFormatter.format('dismiss'));` against the '@react-aria/overlays' registry (line 28). patches/react-aria@3.51.0.patch adds dist/private/intl/overlays/fa-IR.mjs with `"dismiss": "بستن"` and registers it in that registry. Lumo already ships this; overlays.test.tsx:221 pins the unpatched-locale count at two.
the_decisive_comparison.the_difference_in_one_sentence: In React Aria the string has an ADDRESS — namespace '@react-aria/overlays', key 'dismiss' — so a patch adds a LOCALE beside 34 others and everything else keeps working; in Base UI the string has no address, so the only remedy is rewriting a literal inside a component file.
why_a_byte_patch_is_not_equivalent: It cannot be locale-aware. No locale is in scope at that line — ComboboxInternalDismissButton imports only useMergedRefs, visuallyHiddenInput, useButton, createChangeEventDetails, REASONS and useComboboxRootContext, and Combobox.Root's own `locale` prop is documented as being for string COMPARISON (AriaCombobox.d.ts:206) and is consumed by useFilter, never reaching this component. Patching 'Dismiss' to 'بستن' therefore hardcodes Persian for every locale the codebase will ever serve, English included. React Aria's patch adds a locale; this one REPLACES the string.

There is nothing to validate against. A bundle patch can be checked — does key 'dismiss' still exist in namespace '@react-aria/overlays'? A literal patch can only be checked by the patch applying, and a patch that fails to apply is a loud error while a patch that applies to a moved literal is a silent one.

It is not a supported extension point, so it carries no compatibility promise across minors. The bundle registry is the library's own documented mechanism; the literal is an implementation detail of an @internal file.

taxonomy_comparison.caveat: Different scopes. Read the scoped row, not the totals row, for a like-for-like number.

react-aria.note: not measured at whole-library scope; RAC ships far more components than Lumo swept

thirteen_file_experiment_scope.files: experiments/baseline-rac/ — button, checkbox, combobox, dialog, menu, number-field, popover, select, slider, switch, tabs, toggle, tooltip
thirteen_file_experiment_scope.note: The three outside this scope are progress (1), meter (0) and toast (1).

what_base_ui_is_better_at: Seven of eight reach a prop, versus five of eight for React Aria at its own sweep scope. Base UI's philosophy is that it announces almost nothing by default, and where it does the escape hatch is the ordinary props path with a stated precedence rule (merge-props/mergeProps.mjs:118).

No LocalizedStringProvider trap. DECISIONS.md §0.1 records that React Aria's provider renders no children and only sets a window global, so its dictionary reaches nothing during renderToStaticMarkup. Base UI has no such thing to be misled by; the props that reach these strings are ordinary props and they work identically on the server.
It ships zero validation copy of its own — field errors come from element.validationMessage, so Base UI never puts an untranslatable sentence in a form.

Its default-nothing stance means several components a consumer would expect to leak do not: Select, Menu, Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Tabs, Checkbox, Switch, Toggle and Button emit no English at all, and Combobox.ChipRemove emits an unnamed <button> rather than an English-named one. That is a different defect class (Lumo's required-label rule already covers it) but it is not an English leak.
Meter's default aria-valuetext is pure formatted number (aria-valuetext="۴۰٪"), with no prose wrapper to leak.
what_base_ui_is_worse_at: The unreachable Dismiss, which is the whole answer to the brief's question.

No locale provider: four components each need their own `locale` prop and the default is the machine's locale, so a Persian page renders Latin digits by omission rather than by error. React Aria's I18nProvider is one lever at the root.
Direction is a second, independent, LTR-defaulting lever with no relationship to locale or to <html dir>, and it changes server output (SliderThumb.mjs:225).
One half-localised string — '۲۰ start range' — which is the hardest kind to notice, because the Persian half is what a reviewer looks at.
getAriaValueText sits on Slider.Thumb but reads like a Root concern; aimed at Root it silently does nothing.

aria_attribute_census.note: Every aria-* attribute NAME in the dist, by occurrence count in .mjs. Included so a later phase can see the surface without rescanning.

aria_attrs_assigned_a_string_literal.kind: test fixture — shipped in the package but reachable only from Base UI's own test helper, not from any component

not_counted_as_announced.why: an emoji, announced by the screen reader in the READER's language, not the library's. It is rendered content a consumer replaces, not a string the library speaks.

not_counted_as_announced.what: progress/root/ProgressRoot.mjs:70 and meter/root/MeterRoot.mjs:57 — a visually hidden x
not_counted_as_announced.why: role=presentation removes it from the accessibility tree. It is a Latin character in the DOM of a Persian page and worth knowing about, but it is not announced and Lumo's no-latin-digits rule does not see a letter.

dist_shape.note: The dist is unminified per-component ESM/CJS, one directory per part, so every string quoted here is readable in the installed package without a sourcemap.
